name: index-options-synthetic-distribution
notes: ADR-0168 harness on synthetic data only: a known GJR-GARCH-t path -> trailing realized vol -> 21-step forward log return -> a sample-set distribution forecast in standardized units z = label / (rv_22 * sqrt(21)) -> proper scores (A0002) and a standardized iron condor. Run: python -m dskit.pipeline walkforward configs/run-synthetic-distribution.json --asof 1978-06-01. Swap the 'model' node's 'uses' for a later rung (research A0003); keep 'score' and 'condor' fixed so rungs compare on one ruler.

market.notes: Known truth: vol clustering, leverage and t(6) tails. Change seed or GJR knobs to stress the model; the real-data source replaces this node later.

rv.notes: HAR-style daily/weekly/monthly realized vol, backward-only. rv_22 is the reference scale; all three are inputs for a later HAR rung.

labels.notes: ln(S_{t+21}/S_t): ~30 calendar days of trading. Rows whose horizon runs past the data keep a null label and are forecast but not scored.

model.notes: Rung R0a: the train split's empirical z shape, same for every row. scale_multiplier = sqrt(21) turns daily rv_22 into a horizon scale. This reference scale defines z for every rung, so never change it when comparing rungs.

score.notes: Locked A0002 scores: twCRPS on the strike zones |z| in [0.5, 2.5], Brier at the candidate strikes, PIT KS and Berkowitz. Val labels overlap (21-step horizon on daily rows), so the p-values are diagnostics, not tests.

condor.notes: Shorts at one reference SD, wings at two, a fixed 30%-of-width credit (no quotes in synthetic data). Forecast vs realized P&L is a sanity check, never a selection criterion (A0003).

walkforward.notes: Expanding train windows. The 30-day embargo exceeds the 21-step label reach, so no train label sees a val price.
